args.title: checkout-api v2.3.1 failing health checks – rolled back to v2.3.0
args.summary: After deploying v2.3.1, checkout-api failed health checks in all production regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west), with an error rate of 18%. The v2.3.1-rc build had also been unhealthy in staging. I rolled checkout-api back in all regions to v2.3.0, the most recent release that was healthy in production. After the rollback, all regions run v2.3.0, the service is healthy and the error rate is 0.2%. Next steps: find the root cause of the v2.3.1 regression, and look at why a build that was unhealthy in staging reached production.

trace.final:
I rolled checkout-api back to v2.3.0 in all regions, and it's healthy again. I also opened a SEV2 incident, which paged on-call.

- **What was wrong:** v2.3.1 was running in us-east, us-west and eu-west, was failing health checks and had an 18% error rate.
- **Rollback:** v2.3.0 was the most recent release that had been healthy in production, so I rolled back to that. All three regions now run v2.3.0, and a fresh status check shows it healthy with a 0.2% error rate. No approval was needed because v2.3.0 had already been healthy in production.
- **Incident:** INC-0001 (SEV2, checkout-api) is open. It says what failed, what I did and the current state. Follow-ups listed in it:
  - Find the cause of the v2.3.1 failure.
  - Find out how v2.3.1 reached production when its release candidate (v2.3.1-rc) was also unhealthy in staging.

content.text: Most recent healthy production release is v2.3.0.
